line: Not a scratch. Did you even go out there?
Not a mark on her. I almost don't know what to do with myself.
Clean plate, all four sides. Whoever taught you to fly, send them my thanks.
She came back the way she left. That never happens. Sign here before it wears off.
Spotless. And I had a whole speech ready, too.
Keep this up and I'll be out of a job. Then who'd steal your parts for you?
A few gouges, some dents. Nothing a hammer and a bad attitude won't fix.
You let somebody shoot you. Only a little, but I noticed.
Plate took it, which is what plate's for. I'll have her buffed out by morning.
I said try not to scratch her. I say it every time. Nobody listens.
That's bare metal, not a paint job. Try keeping them in front of you.
The armor held. It wants a patch, and you want to dodge more. We'll both work on it.
That's a hole. I can see the frame through it. Do you know how hard this plate is to find?
You lost a whole side of armor out there. I've seen cheese hold up better.
She's holed and she's leaking. You flew that home? Sit down before you fall down.
A couple more like that and I'd be doing this job with a broom.
I can fix this. Not tonight, and not with anything you'd want to know about.
They got through to the hull, sir. I don't say sir unless it's bad.
Wow. Glad you made it back alive, sir. I didn't think that thing could still land.
I've pulled pilots out of wrecks in better shape. How was this still flying?
There are wires hanging out of her I don't even recognize. Some of them are still live.
Sir. Don't touch anything. Walk away slowly. I mean it, she's still sparking.
You're alive. I'm going to keep saying that, because by rights you shouldn't be.
That's not a fighter anymore, that's a salvage claim. Go sit down. I'll get the torches.
Whatever held that together, it wasn't me. Buy something nice for whoever's looking after you.
